description.narrative: Farmers in Tunisia have limited skills to effectively implement water-saving solutions. While there is strong interest among farmers to adopt water-smart technologies, they often lack the practical knowledge, technical support, and financial means to do so.Another chronic and structural problem is youth unemployment in Tunisia. Tunisia has a very large, young adult population and lacks decent jobs and business opportunities. More than 40% of young Tunisians (aged 15-24) in rural areas are unemployed. Agriculture, often the only sector offering employment, is perceived as unattractive by youth due to outdated practices. Long-term unemployment of youth in rural areas fuels discontent, radicalisation or even decisions to migrate.The adoption of water-smart technologies in Tunisia’s agricultural sector would not only be crucial for effective water resource management but also has the potential to create much needed jobs in rural areas. Water technology has the potential to create jobs that are attractive for youth, especially the ones that are living in rural areas. Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) centers, such as the Agricultural Extension and Training Agency (AVFA) being the biggest TVET institution in Tunisia, could play an important role in capacity building of youth and farmers with regards to water smart management. Several Agence de la Vulgarisation et de la Formation Agricoles (AVFA) centers have expressed a clear desire to play a more prominent role in demonstrating such technologies and training both students and farmers in smart irrigation systems. However, they currently lack the necessary connections to technology providers, as well as the equipment and skilled instructors to deliver practical, technical training on the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of water-saving technologies. To make farmers more water-resilient, create rural employment opportunities and foster the adoption of Dutch water-smart solutions in Tunisia, a multifaceted approach is proposed with this project.The Water Smart Tunisia project would like to build on partnerships and former experiences, using TVET as a vehicle for creating Dutch trade opportunities, water-resilience, and jobs for rural youth by establishing an ecosystem where Dutch water smart technologies are more widely adopted, jobs are created for rural youth, and Tunisia’s farmers become more resilient to water scarcity. This will be achieved by facilitating partnerships between Dutch technology suppliers and local partners, by turning two TVET centres into demonstration and training hubs on water-smart irrigation technologies and by equipping local youth and farmers with knowledge and skills on these systems and technologies. The project will be co-funded by Swiss Contact and the TVET institution AFVA.
